offerings.substitution_reason: Cloudflare's entire Qwen catalog is three models - qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct, qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8 and qwen3-embedding-0.6b - and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct is none of them. qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct is the code-specialised Qwen Cloudflare does serve: a different generation and a dense 32B rather than a 30B MoE, so it covers the coding capability under its own name and its own evidence. It is not Qwen3-Coder and no measurement taken on it may be recorded against Qwen3-Coder.

Cloudflare serves the 32B distill of DeepSeek-R1, not the 7B. Same distillation family and the same reasoning capability, a different model at four times the size. The 7B is the candidate because it fits this host; the 32B exists only on the provider, so the two are not interchangeable evidence in either direction.

providers.notes: A hosted catalog, and that is the load-bearing limit. It serves models Cloudflare has published under @cf/ ids; there is no documented path for uploading our own GGUF, and the only weight customisation on a model page is a `lora` adapter name against a Cloudflare-hosted base. So this path can answer a capability, but it can never run an artifact we admitted. Billing is impossible on the Workers Free plan - the pricing table records "N/A - Upgrade to Workers Paid" for it - so exhausting the allowance fails the request instead of charging. Some resource-intensive models are Paid-only and return 403 / internal error 5035 on Free; that list is recorded per model, not assumed.

catalog_check.why: Cloudflare's Qwen catalog was read in full and contains no Qwen3-8B. It runs on this host anyway, at a measured 8655 MB peak.
